transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I've been really struggling with making careless mistakes and failing to pay attention to details at work. I also feel this constant restlessness, like I'm always "on the go," and it's been happening for about ten months now.
Did you have similar problems with attention, careless mistakes, or feeling restless when you were a child, such as at school or at home? Or did these symptoms only start in the past year?

Actually, I've struggled with attention and feeling restless since I was a kid in elementary school, definitely before I was 12. But it has become consistently troublesome and much harder to manage over the last 10 months.
Do you also find yourself worrying excessively about many different things most days, and is that worry hard to control? Or is the main problem more your lifelong inattention and restlessness?

No, I wouldn't say I experience excessive or uncontrollable worrying about things. The main issue is definitely my long-standing difficulty with paying attention and constantly feeling restless or "on the go."
Do these attention and restlessness problems affect you in more than one setting, such as both at work and at home or in relationships? Can you give a brief example?
Honestly, I haven't really thought about how these issues impact those specific areas like my home life or relationships yet. I've mostly just been focused on the problems it's causing me at work.
Besides trouble paying attention, do you also often interrupt others, blurt things out, or act impulsively? Or is it mostly inattention without those hyperactive or impulsive behaviors?

Yes, I definitely have those hyperactive and impulsive behaviors too. I often blurt out answers before people even finish their questions, and I constantly feel restless. I always feel "on the go," almost like I'm driven by a motor.
Besides careless mistakes, do you also often have trouble sustaining attention, seem not to listen, fail to finish tasks, lose things, get easily distracted, or forget daily activities?

I definitely struggle a lot with sustaining my attention, especially when I have to read long documents or sit through lengthy meetings where I just lose focus. As for losing things, forgetting daily tasks, or not listening, I don't really notice those being much of an issue for me.
Do you also often have trouble organizing tasks, avoid or put off tasks that need a lot of mental effort, or get easily distracted by things going on around you?

I definitely tend to put off or avoid tasks that require a lot of mental effort, mostly because they feel so draining and I dread having to concentrate that hard. As for organizing my tasks or getting easily distracted by my surroundings, those aren't really much of an issue for me.
Besides feeling restless and blurting things out, do you also often fidget, have trouble staying seated, talk excessively, have trouble waiting your turn, or interrupt other people?

No, I don't really struggle with those specific things. I don't have trouble with fidgeting, staying seated, or talking excessively, and waiting my turn or interrupting others isn't really an issue for me.
Outside of work, do these attention or restlessness problems also cause difficulties at home, in daily responsibilities, or in relationships? Even one clear example would help.

I guess at home I really struggle with avoiding tasks that require a lot of mental effort, like trying to budget or plan out chores. Also, my family sometimes gets annoyed when I blurt out answers before they're done talking to me.
When you start chores, paperwork, or other responsibilities at home, do you often leave them unfinished because you lose focus or get sidetracked?

Yes, I definitely leave chores and paperwork unfinished all the time. I always start them with good intentions, but I quickly lose focus, get sidetracked, and struggle to sustain the mental effort needed to actually finish them.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding pattern since childhood, with onset before age 12, of both inattentive symptoms and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms. Inattention is supported by careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining attention, avoidance of tasks requiring sustained mental effort, and failure to finish chores/paperwork due to losing focus. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are supported by blurting out answers, persistent restlessness, and feeling constantly 'on the go' or 'driven by a motor.' Symptoms have been present for about 10 months in their currently impairing form, occur in more than one setting (work and home), and cause functional impairment.
